newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian stocks barely moved at opening.
newsitem.headline: Australian stocks barely moved at opening.

text.p: The Australian share market was little changed at the opening on Thursday with inconclusive finishes in offshore markets failing to provide any guidance.
The All Ordinaries index was up 0.1 points at 2,585.3.
The market quickly settled into a tight range with brokers saying little real trend was apparent.
A repeat of Wednesday's single figure finish was expected.
"It's drifting at the moment," said Nevitts Ltd senior dealer Jim Tredenick, noting the lack of clear signals from offshore. "It was all pretty steady overseas," he said.
With the mixed showing among the leaders, attention turned elsewhere with second tier oil stocks enjoying the spotlight.

Cultus Petroleum added over nine percent to a record high A$4.05 (US$3.08) before easing back to A$3.95 by 10.45 a.m. (0045 GMT). Tap Oil jumped over four percent to a record high A$1.75. Oil Search Ltd completed a hat trick of record highs in the sector, jumping three percent to a record A$3.21.
Elsewhere, retailer Coles Myer slid nearly three percent to A$6.12 amid selling after its annual analyst briefing.
Rises outnumbered falls by a ratio of about three to two, while about 44 percent of stocks traded remained steady.
